newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese media mum on crisis in own backyard.
newsitem.headline: Chinese media mum on crisis in own backyard.

text.p: The defection of a top North Korean official to arch-enemy South Korea has captured headlines around the world, with one notable exception: China, where the dramatic Cold War crisis is playing itself out.
Foreign reporters have mounted a 24-hour watch on Seoul's consular compound where Hwang Jang-yop, Pyongyang's top ideologue and senior aide to leader Kim Jong-il, is holed up.
China's state-run media have ignored the drama unfolding in their capital.
North Korea's domestic media also maintained their silence on the defection, media monitors in Japan said.

The North's official news agency, whose services are available only outside the country, has said nothing since it reported the Pyongyang Foreign Ministry's angry response to Seoul's announcement of Hwang's defection on Wednesday.

In Beijing, a bullet-proof car and a crowd-control truck fitted with a water cannon remain outside the compound entrance and dozens of police armed with assault rifles stand guard in what would be a sure draw for reporters in nearly any other nation.

"Maybe someone should call CCTV (China Central Television) and tip them off that there's a story here," joked one foreign cameraman standing vigil near the compound on a tree-lined lane in Beijing's sedate diplomatic quarter.
Curious passers-by and frustrated visa-seekers have tried to glean from foreign reporters news of the crisis that has shut down the consular office since Hwang sought refuge there last Wednesday.
"Any new developments today?" asked one woman who travelled from the northeastern province of Jilin in hopes of obtaining a visa to visit relatives in South Korea.

Hwang has become the focus of a Cold War row between the two Koreas, enemies since their 1950-53 war ended only in a truce -- and a big embarrassment to China, which must decide how to usher him out of Beijing without offending an old socialist comrade or a new capitalist friend.
